title: Sep 10 Results: Tough Day on the Mound
summary: Sep 10 predictions went 2-3 with a 40% hit rate - breaking down what went wrong

content.value:
## The Reality Check

Look, I'm not going to sugarcoat it - today was rough. Going 2-3 with a 40% accuracy rate is the kind of outing where you tip your cap to the opposition and head back to the film room. From a pitcher's perspective, days like this remind me of those starts where your stuff just isn't fooling anybody. Let's break down what happened.

## The Three Misses

Three picks that didn't land, and all three were relatively close probability calls. When you're pitching with margins this tight, one bad sequence changes everything.

## What the Numbers Tell Us

Here's the thing about those three misses - none of them were high-confidence calls. The Phillies pick was essentially a coin flip at 50%, and both the Rays and Rangers were sitting at 54%. In baseball terms, that's like facing a hitter with a .270 average - you've got the edge, but it's no guarantee.

The two hits came from our stronger conviction plays: Yankees at 61% and Pirates at 59%. When we had better separation in the probabilities, the model performed. That's a key takeaway.

## The Pitcher's Analysis

From my years on the mound, I learned that you can't win them all. What matters is the process. Today's misses weren't blowouts in terms of probability - they were tight games where variance played its hand. The Astros-Phillies game being a 50-50 call? That's telling you right there that either team could take it.

The important thing is our higher-confidence picks (Yankees and Pirates, both near 60%) came through. That's where the real edge lives.

## The Game Plan Moving Forward

With no games tomorrow, it's a perfect time to regroup. In my playing days, off-days were for reviewing mechanics and game-planning. Same principle applies here.

We'll be back with fresh picks when the schedule resumes. Keep grinding, trust the process, and remember - even the best pitchers give up runs. It's about limiting the damage and coming back stronger.

**Stay locked in.**

— Ace
